children: A targeted U.S. diesel export restriction could provide some near-term relief to domestic fuel prices while avoiding the disruption of a complete export ban, says Michelle Brouhard from Kpler. Export controls would be more complicated to administer than a blanket ban, requiring Washington to determine and monitor volumes, licenses, exemptions and, potentially, destinations. At the same time, they would give policymakers greater flexibility over how many barrels remain in the U.S. and which foreign buyers retain access. According to Kpler, limiting exports by 500,000 barrels a day, rather than the full 1.2 million barrels a day, would leave more fuel in the U.S. market while allowing roughly 700,000 barrels a day to continue reaching overseas buyers. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
